fact: WHO's country office report for 2024-2025 describes DHIS2 as the Government's selected 'gold standard' platform for aggregate data, used to monitor HIV/PMTCT, RMNCAHA and immunisation across districts.

WHO's 2024-2025 report lists heavy reliance on paper-based reporting by facilities as a challenge and recommends revising the DHIS2 dashboards and trackers 'to enable onsite data capturing', so entry is not at the facility; the report does not name the level at which the paper reports are keyed (no figures given).

The Data Landscapers 54-country review (an AI-assisted compilation, the author's analysis) states that DHIS2 is deployed nationally for aggregate reporting but data is typically collected on paper at facilities and entered later at district level; no date is given, so the published date is used.

fact: The Assistant Minister of Health told Parliament on 5 March 2026 that Phase 1 of the centralised Electronic Medical Record had been implemented in 22 health facilities in Ngami, to be extended to 21 facilities in Okavango by end of March 2026; the facility types and a national denominator are not given.

The Ministry of Health's 2026/27 budget speech reports the Phase 1 rollout of the centralised EMR as ongoing, at 22 facilities in Ngami to date, 21 more in Okavango due by end of March 2026 and the remaining 29 districts planned for the 2026/27 financial year.

The Ministry of Health's 2026/27 budget speech states that the Ministry of Health and the Ministry of Local Government and Traditional Affairs will jointly roll out the completed EMR system to the remaining 29 districts in 2026/27.

The 2026/27 development budget request allocates P62,534,000 to the Ministry of Health headquarters for consultancies, computerisation and fleet, naming the 'Digitalization of Health Services Project' among what it funds; the EMR rollout is reported under the speech's 'Digitalisation of Health Services' heading, and the line does not name the EMR itself.

The Minister of Local Government and Traditional Affairs told Parliament on 19 November 2025 that the Electronic Medical Records system was being piloted in two districts; no facility count or denominator is given.

The Minister of Local Government and Traditional Affairs told Parliament on 19 November 2025 that his ministry was advancing the development of integrated systems including the Electronic Medical Records, to link to the Botswana Health Information Exchange.

A literature review in BMC Medical Informatics and Decision Making found that 11 of the 12 African countries studied (92%), Botswana among them and Malawi the only exception, had no national health information strategy for their DHIS-based data warehouse, only strategies run under donor-funded projects; the review was carried out in February to July 2019 and gives no date for the finding, so the published date is used.
